title: Adapt the Object to the Subject: Representative Study Material for Empirical Software Engineering
title_zh: 使对象适应主体：实证软件工程的代表性研究材料

paragraphs.en: 研究提出用LLM生成上下文自适应合成需求，提高实验中研究对象的感知代表性。 External validity is a central concern in empirical software engineering, yet the debate has largely focused on whether study participants are representative. How well the study objects they reason about - code, models, or requirements - are representative of each participant's own work is often overlooked. Practitioners' own artifacts would be ideal, but are often out of reach, so researchers sample from public datasets or construct objects artificially. Whether this lack of subject-object fit affects participants' ability to act on the material remains unknown. We take a first step toward answering this question for requirements. We propose an approach that uses an LLM to generate context-adapted synthetic requirements just-in-time during an online survey from a short, participant-supplied context description, optionally injecting requirements smells as controlled stimuli. To validate the approach, we conducted a controlled experiment with 31 industry practitioners in a 2x2 design that crosses stimulus generation (static vs. synthetic) with quality (clean vs. smelly). Each participant rated the perceived representativeness and assessability of 20 requirements. Using Bayesian data analysis within a statistical causal-inference framework, we find that perceived representativeness has a strong positive effect on assessability. Synthetic requirements are rated as more representative and, primarily due to this gain, more assessable than static ones sourced from public datasets; smell injection leaves both perceptions unchanged. Our results support treating a lack of study-object representativeness as a first-class validity threat and position context-adapted synthetic study objects as a practical addition to the empirical methodology toolbox.
paragraphs.zh: 研究提出用LLM生成上下文自适应合成需求，提高实验中研究对象的感知代表性。外部效度是实证软件工程中的核心关注点，但相关讨论大多集中于研究参与者是否具有代表性。 研究所涉及的研究对象——代码、模型或需求——在多大程度上能代表每位参与者自身的工作，却常常被忽视。 从业者自己的制品虽然是最理想的，但往往难以获取，因此研究者只能从公开数据集中抽样或人工构造研究对象。 这种“主体-对象”不匹配是否会影响参与者对材料进行处理的能力，目前尚不清楚。 我们以需求为对象，朝回答这一问题迈出了第一步。 我们提出一种方法，在在线调查过程中，基于参与者提供的简短上下文描述，利用LLM即时生成上下文自适应的合成需求，并可选地注入需求坏味道作为受控刺激。 为验证该方法，我们在2×2设计中开展了一项受控实验，将刺激生成方式（静态 vs. 合成）与质量（干净 vs. 含坏味道）进行交叉组合，共有31名行业从业者参与。 每位参与者对20条需求的感知代表性和可评估性进行了评分。 通过在统计因果推断框架内进行贝叶斯数据分析，我们发现感知代表性对可评估性有很强的正向影响。 与来自公开数据集的静态需求相比，合成需求被评价为更具代表性，并且主要由于这一优势而更具可评估性；坏味道注入对这两种感知均无影响。 我们的结果支持将研究对象代表性不足视为一等效度威胁，并将上下文自适应的合成研究对象定位为实证方法学工具箱中的一种实用补充。
